pages.text:
Welcome to Spellweaver2! This mod's magic system consists of two parts working together:

$(l)· Node Tree$(): The skeleton of spells, determining "when to do what" — sequential execution, loops, conditional branches, waits.

$(l)· Rune Stack$(): The flesh of spells, determining "how data flows" — each rune takes data from the top of the stack, processes it, and puts it back, completing calculations like an assembly line.

Don't worry, it's much simpler than it sounds. Follow the guide below, and you'll soon be creating your own spells.

$(l)What is a Stack?$()

A stack is like a pile of plates: you can only place new plates on top (push), and you can only take plates from the top (pop). When spells execute, all data flows on this "pile of plates".

$(l)What is a Tree?$()

Spell nodes are like an inverted tree. The root is at the top, branching downward. Each node has its own responsibility: $(9)Normal Node$() stores rune sequences, $(9)Loop Node$() repeats execution of child nodes, $(9)Condition Node$() decides whether to execute based on conditions, $(9)Wait Node$() pauses the spell for a period.

Nodes execute sequentially — one completes before the next begins — just like processes on an assembly line. For now, just keep this in mind; it's easy to understand in practice.

$(l)How to Write the Simplest Spell?$()

Press O to open the $(9)Spell Editor$(). You'll see a rotating magic circle in the center, which we call the $(9)Central Node$(). Right-click the central node, select "$(9)Add Normal Node$()" from the menu, then left-click the newly created normal node to enter the rune drawing interface.

Tips: Cursor position in both rune and spell editors can be adjusted using left/right arrow keys and right mouse button

$(l)Start writing spells!$()

$(l)Your First Spell: Break the Block Below$()

Let's start with a spell that produces an immediate visual effect — breaking the block you're standing on.

Rune Sequence:
$(9)$(l)Self FootCoordinate Break$()

$(l)Execution Process:$()
·$(9)Self$() → pushes yourself (player entity) onto the stack
·$(9)FootCoordinate$() → pops player, pushes block coordinate beneath feet
·$(9)Break$() → pops coordinate, consumes mana to break the block

Try standing on dirt or stone!
